newsitem.title: BRAZIL: BRAZIL'S LEFT TRIES TO STOP OIL LAW IN HIGH COURT.
newsitem.headline: BRAZIL'S LEFT TRIES TO STOP OIL LAW IN HIGH COURT.

text.p: A group of left-wing Brazilian political parties have launched a high court challenge to a new law that opens up the country's oil and gas sectors, a lawmaker said Wednesday.

Workers Party (PT) congressman Luciano Zica said the law violated Brazil's constitution by allowing state-owned petroleum giant Petrobras to form new subsidiaries without seeking specific approval from Congress on each occasion.
The article would enable the government to offer private groups controlling stakes in existing Petrobras assets, such as refineries and transportation infrastructure, Zica said.
"It would be a privatization of Petrobras by the back door" he said.
The PT and three other parties asked the Supreme Federal Tribunal (STF), Brazil's highest court for constitutional matters, to strike down the article in a case brought Wednesday, he said.

Brazil's left-wing opposition opposed the new law at every stage of its passage through Congress. The law, which was signed by President Fernando Henrique Cardoso last week, allows private companies to compete or enter partnerships with Petrobras.
Earlier this year, left-wing opposition parties sought and failed to stop the privatization of Brazil's telecommunications industry by taking legal action at the STF.
